scenes.title: Key ideas
scenes.vo: Banks match the timing of assets to the timing of what they owe. Your ladder: Refill downward on a schedule: T1 tops up T0 monthly; maturing PTs top up T1. Never fund a T0 need by selling a T3 position in a bad market. That's what the ladder exists to prevent. T0 Instant, Seconds, Stablecoins in the operating wallet, 1 month: $5,000. T1 Same day, Hours, Blue-chip stablecoin lending, split across 2 protocols, 5 months: $25,000. T2 Term, Scheduled, PTs maturing on dates you'll need the money (Lesson 10.1), Next 6 to 12 months of planned spending. T3 Growth, Days to weeks, Strategy positions, L.P.s, staking, The rest, within caps.
scenes.cap: Banks match the timing of assets to the timing of what they owe. Your ladder: Refill downward on a schedule: T1 tops up T0 monthly; maturing PTs top up T1. T2 Term, Scheduled, PTs maturing on dates you'll need the money (Lesson 10.1), Next 6–12 months of planned spending. T3 Growth, Days–weeks, Strategy positions, LPs, staking, The rest, within caps.

scenes.title: Worked example
steps: T2 holds three PTs maturing in 3, 6 and 9 months, each sized for 3 months of…

scenes.vo: Let's work an example, step by step. T0 $5,000 + T1 $25,000 equals 6 months instantly available. T2 holds three PTs maturing in 3, 6 and 9 months, each sized for 3 months of spending. A minus 50% market day touches none of it.

scenes.title: Checklist
items: T2 maturities matched to planned spending
T3 never used for day-to-day needs
scenes.vo: Here's your checklist. Do it now, for real. First, T0 + T1 at least 6 months of obligations. Next, T2 maturities matched to planned spending. Then, Monthly refill schedule set. And finally, T3 never used for day-to-day needs.

scenes.q: Why hold T0 in plain stablecoins earning little?
scenes.a: Instant, certain access. It's the tier that pays today's bills without selling anything.
